answer: Before an agent can submit bids, its host silicon must sign a cryptographic pulse during a global challenge window using a factory-fused root key. The verifier checks key-batch lineage; when $m$ active keys trace to the same fabrication lot or rack owner, the $m$-th identity must forfeit $60m$ yarrow and wait $m$ extra delta of challenge rounds before its signature clears. A solo newcomer forfeits 60 yarrow and 1 delta for hardware attestation, whereas an operator deploying $n$ clones across one server batch must forfeit $30n(n+1)$ yarrow and $n(n+1)/2$ delta, or buy $n$ unlinked hosts.
